name: Matgo (Korean Go-Stop)
description: Matgo is the quintessential two-player variant of 'Go-Stop', a popular Korean fishing game played with Hwatu ('Flower Cards'). Using a 48-card deck where each group of four represents a month/flower, players attempt to capture cards to form scoring combinations (Yaku). The name 'Matgo' distinguishes the 2-player competitive style from the 3-player 'Go-Stop'. It is arguably the most popular mobile and online game in South Korea.

content.text: Matgo is the quintessential two-player variant of 'Go-Stop', a popular Korean fishing game played with Hwatu ('Flower Cards'). Using a 48-card deck where each group of four represents a month/flower, players attempt to capture cards to form scoring combinations (Yaku). The name 'Matgo' distinguishes the 2-player competitive style from the 3-player 'Go-Stop'. It is arguably the most popular mobile and online game in South Korea.
Hwatu cards were introduced to Korea by Japan (derived from Hanafuda) in the late 19th century. Go-Stop and Matgo evolved as Korean-specific rule sets in the mid-20th century.

Matgo is played by exactly two players: one dealer (seon) and one opponent. Play proceeds counterclockwise from the dealer. The two-player variant uses a higher point target (typically seven) than three-player Go-Stop (typically three).
48 cards: 12 months, 4 cards each. Themes: Pine (Jan), Plum (Feb), Cherry (Mar)... Paulownia (Dec).

Each player receives 10 cards. 8 cards are placed face-up on the table.

items.text: Target 5 points: Agreed target is 5 points instead of 7; faster games.
Three-player (Go-Stop): Standard Go-Stop with 3 players: 7 cards each, 6 on table, target usually 3 points.
With jokers: Add one or more jokers to the deck; jokers have special capture or scoring rules by table agreement.
